title: Strategic Alignment
options: Increase the annual maintenance budget.
Review organizational objectives and align the FM strategy.
Replace outdated maintenance equipment.
Outsource all maintenance activities.
question: An organization plans to expand its operations, but FM continues using a maintenance strategy developed five years ago. What should the Facility Manager do FIRST?
explanation: Align FM strategy with organizational goals.

title: Conflict Management
options: Reassign one supervisor immediately.
Escalate the disagreement to Human Resources.
Issue formal warnings to both supervisors.
Facilitate discussion, identify causes, and agree on a resolution.
question: Two FM supervisors disagree about resource allocation, delaying critical maintenance activities. What is the BEST leadership response?
explanation: Resolve the underlying conflict through constructive engagement.

title: Change Management
options: Identify concerns, engage users, and develop a change-management plan.
Require immediate use and penalize noncompliance.
Cancel implementation until technicians agree.
Assign all system activities to IT.
question: Management introduces a new CAFM system, but technicians resist using it. What should the FM Manager do FIRST?
explanation: Understand resistance and manage the transition.

title: Team Development
options: Increase supervision during each maintenance shift.
Replace technicians with specialist subcontractors.
Conduct a competency gap assessment and implement targeted training.
Reduce the complexity of assigned maintenance tasks.
question: An FM department regularly misses performance targets because technicians lack skills required for modern building systems. What is the MOST appropriate action?
explanation: Identify skill gaps before selecting training solutions.

title: Leadership During Budget Cuts
options: Reduce manpower across all facilities equally.
Evaluate service priorities, risks, and efficiency opportunities.
Postpone all preventive maintenance activities.
Reduce service frequencies without informing stakeholders.
question: Senior management announces a 15% reduction in the FM operating budget while expecting service standards to remain unchanged. What should the FM Manager do FIRST?
explanation: Prioritize services using risk and business impact.

title: Executive Priorities
options: An immediate equal cut across all maintenance budgets
A proposal to eliminate all outsourced contracts
A strategy connecting reliability risks, service outcomes, and cost
A plan to postpone reporting until next year
question: A new CEO wants the FM team to focus only on reducing expenditure, although critical sites have experienced rising outages. What should the FM leader present?
explanation: Link resource decisions to organizational goals and material service risks.

title: Delegation and Accountability
options: Clarify delegated responsibilities and retain management oversight
Allow the contractor to define all acceptance criteria
Remove inspection records from the FM reporting process
Wait until an audit identifies a deficiency
question: A facility manager delegates fire-system inspections to a supervisor, who assumes the contractor is solely accountable. What is the BEST response?
explanation: Delegation of tasks does not remove the need for clear accountability and oversight.

title: Stakeholder Resistance
options: Proceed because the budget is approved
Cancel all relocation activities permanently
Ask security to enforce the relocation date
Engage departments, validate needs, and reassess implementation impacts
question: An office relocation is approved, but department heads oppose the new space plan because operational needs were not considered. What should the FM leader do NEXT?
explanation: Stakeholder engagement and change planning support adoption and service continuity.

title: Performance Coaching
options: Issue a written warning immediately
Discuss performance expectations, obstacles, and support needs
Remove the supervisor from all responsibilities
Transfer the problem to procurement
question: A previously strong supervisor begins missing deadlines after a change in responsibilities. What is the MOST constructive first response?
explanation: Coaching starts with understanding performance gaps and agreeing on improvements.

title: FM Policy Change
options: Let each site interpret the requirement independently
Stop all operations until every procedure is rewritten
Set a consistent policy, communicate changes, and verify adoption
Delegate the entire matter to the lowest-priced vendor
question: A new regulatory requirement affects several facilities, but local teams apply inconsistent procedures. What should the FM director prioritize?
explanation: Consistent governance and communication enable compliant execution.
